headline: Southborough boards set warrant articles for Special Town Meeting, launched reviews for a proposed Costco, and narrowed Neary School building options.
synopsis: In September, Southborough boards focused on finalizing warrant articles for the October Special Town Meeting, revealing deep divisions over Community Preservation Act funding for golf course irrigation and a pedestrian trail bridge. The Planning Board opened public hearings on a proposed 167,000-square-foot Costco warehouse and 30-dispenser fueling station along Coslin Drive, drawing resident and board questions regarding regional traffic and noise. Meanwhile, the Elementary School Building Committee eliminated an exterior addition concept for Neary School and focused design work on courtyard gym additions and maintenance baselines. Town departments also began preparing two-tiered FY28 budget proposals, projecting service and staffing reductions if an anticipated tax override fails. Additionally, the Select Board appointed Amy Berry as interim town clerk, while school committees approved a retroactive market salary adjustment for the superintendent.

top_items.title: Planning Board opens hearing on Coslin Drive Costco proposal
top_items.why: Costco submitted applications for a 167,000-square-foot warehouse and 30-position gas station spanning Southborough and Westborough.
top_items.body: The Planning Board opened public hearings for major site plan approval and special permits for the project on 26.12 acres at 21 Coslin Drive. Representatives outlined the site layout, grading, stormwater wetlands, dark-sky compliant lighting, and traffic generation. Board members and residents questioned consultants on traffic congestion, intersection level of service along Route 9, truck delivery routes, and loading dock noise before the hearing was continued to October 19.

top_items.title: Neary building committee eliminates Option 4, narrows project design
top_items.why: Preliminary cost estimates ranging from $24.4 million to $49.2 million prompted the committee to narrow project designs.
top_items.body: Following review of preliminary cost analyses and site evaluations, the Elementary School Building Committee voted 3-1 to eliminate Option 4, which proposed an exterior gym addition over poor soils and high groundwater. The committee voted 4-0 to direct architects to focus remaining design work on Option 1 (code and maintenance upgrades), Option 3 (interior renovations enclosing the courtyard for a gymnasium), and an analysis of a $15 million baseline scope.

top_items.title: Advisory Committee rejects CPA funding for golf and trails
top_items.why: The Advisory Committee voted 0-7 against recommending CPA funds for both municipal golf course irrigation and the Peninsula Trail footbridge.
top_items.body: Town boards split sharply over Community Preservation Act articles heading to the October 17 Special Town Meeting. While the Community Preservation Committee recommended $433,546 for golf course irrigation and $217,318 for the Peninsula Trail footbridge, the Advisory Committee voted unanimously against both, arguing the golf course should be self-funded and trail costs were too high. The Select Board backed the golf irrigation article 5-0 but opposed the footbridge 1-4.

top_items.title: Boards deliberate two-family dwelling zoning bylaw amendment
top_items.why: The proposed bylaw would eliminate the two-year waiting period to convert a single-family house into a two-family dwelling or build new two-family housing.
top_items.body: Town boards reviewed proposed zoning changes for Article 2 on the Special Town Meeting warrant. The Select Board endorsed the measure 4-1 (and later 5-0 on revised text), while the Zoning Board of Appeals cleared updated wording removing references to duplexes and townhouses. However, the Advisory Committee voted 3-4 against recommending approval over density and municipal service concerns, and the Planning Board continued its public hearing to October 17.

top_items.title: Departments model cuts under potential FY28 override failure
top_items.why: Town administration directed departments to submit two budget scenarios ahead of an anticipated spring Proposition 2 1/2 override vote.
top_items.body: Town boards and departments began assembling FY28 budget requests under dual scenarios. Budget A models level services, while Budget B illustrates zero-increase constraints if an override fails. The Library Board of Trustees reviewed Budget B scenarios eliminating programming, travel, and half of subscriptions, while the Board of Health examined reducing staff hours and travel. Separately, the Personnel Board recommended a 3% COLA plus 2% step increment for a 5% total salary adjustment.

top_items.title: Amy Berry appointed interim town clerk through May 2027
top_items.why: The Select Board unanimously appointed Amy Berry to fill the vacancy left by Jim Hegarty's departure.
top_items.body: The Select Board voted 5-0 to appoint Amy Berry as interim town clerk from October 1, 2026, through May 11, 2027. Berry previously served as Southborough deputy town clerk for six years and as Grafton town clerk. The board also advanced a warrant article for the October Special Town Meeting to transition the town clerk role from an elected office to an appointed position, subject to voter approval at the May 2027 election.

top_items.title: School committees approve salary adjustment for superintendent
top_items.why: Four school committees approved a market correction raising Gregory Martineau's base salary to $270,213 for the 2026-2027 school year.
top_items.body: Following an executive session, the Southborough School Committee, Northborough School Committee, Regional School Committee, and Superintendency Union No. 3 voted to grant Superintendent Gregory Martineau a $22,750 retroactive base salary increase. The committees also unanimously approved Martineau's 2026-2027 evaluation goals, which focus on district leadership transitions and major capital projects, including the Neary School building study.
